note: Induct on n=|X|. Necessity: matched partners of S are distinct elements of N(S). Sufficiency: if every nonempty proper A has |N(A)|>|A|, integrality gives |N(A)|>=|A|+1; choose x in X and y adjacent to x, delete x,y, and check Hall after losing at most y. Otherwise choose nonempty proper A with equality. The induced graph on A and N(A) is Hall. The residual graph on X\A and Y\N(A) is Hall because N(A union C)=N(A) disjoint-union (N(C)\N(A)), so Hall on A union C yields |N_res(C)|>=|C|. Inductive matchings lie on disjoint vertex sets and combine.
